# Run comprehensive data quality check first 
def comprehensive_data_quality_check(df, report_title):
    """
    Performs a comprehensive data quality check on a DataFrame
    """
    print(f"=== {report_title} ===\n")
    
    # Basic dataset information
    print("Dataset Overview:")
    print(f"Shape: {df.shape}")
    print(f"Columns: {list(df.columns)}")
    print()
    
    # Missing values analysis
    print("Missing Values:")
    missing_data = df.isnull().sum()
    missing_percent = (missing_data / len(df)) * 100
    missing_summary = pd.DataFrame({
        'Missing Count': missing_data,
        'Missing Percentage': missing_percent
    })
    print(missing_summary[missing_summary['Missing Count'] > 0])
    print()
    
    # Data types
    print("Data Types:")
    print(df.dtypes)
    print()
    
    # Basic statistics for numerical columns
    print("Numerical Columns Summary:")
    numerical_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns
    if len(numerical_cols) > 0:
        print(df[numerical_cols].describe())
    else:
        print("No numerical columns found")
    print()
    
    # Duplicate rows
    duplicates = df.duplicated().sum()
    print(f"Duplicate Rows: {duplicates}")
    
    return missing_summary

# Now you can call the function (assuming 'df' is your DataFrame)
comprehensive_data_quality_check(df, "Medical Dataset Quality Report")

def comprehensive_data_quality_check(df, report_title):
    """

    """
    print(f"=== {report_title} ===\n")
    
    # Basic dataset information
    print("Dataset Overview:")
    print(f"Shape: {df.shape}")
    print(f"Columns: {list(df.columns)}")
    print()
    
    # Missing values analysis
    print("Missing Values:")
    missing_data = df.isnull().sum()
    missing_percent = (missing_data / len(df)) * 100
    missing_summary = pd.DataFrame({
        'Missing Count': missing_data,
        'Missing Percentage': missing_percent
    })
    print(missing_summary[missing_summary['Missing Count'] > 0])
    print()
    
    # Data types
    print("Data Types:")
    print(df.dtypes)
    print()
    
    # Basic statistics for numerical columns
    print("Numerical Columns Summary:")
    numerical_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns
    if len(numerical_cols) > 0:
        print(df[numerical_cols].describe())
    else:
        print("No numerical columns found")
    print()
    
    # Duplicate rows
    duplicates = df.duplicated().sum()
    print(f"Duplicate Rows: {duplicates}")
    
    return missing_summary

# Age VS Death Flag
def analyze_single_column(df, column_name, target_col='Death Flag', figsize=(15, 10)):
    """
    Perform detailed bivariate analysis between a single column and Death Flag
    with beautiful visualizations and comprehensive statistics
    """
    
    # Set style for better looking plots
    plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8')
    sns.set_palette("husl")
    
    # Create analysis dataframe
    analysis_data = df[[target_col, column_name]].dropna()
    
    # Force Death Flag to be treated as categorical
    target_is_numeric = False  # Always treat Death Flag as categorical
    col_is_numeric = pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(analysis_data[column_name])
    
    print(f"=== DETAILED ANALYSIS: {column_name} vs {target_col} ===")
    print("=" * 60)
    
    # Basic descriptive statistics
    print(f"\nDESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS:")
    print("-" * 30)
    
    if col_is_numeric:
        print(f"{column_name} Statistics:")
        print(f"  Mean: {analysis_data[column_name].mean():.4f}")
        print(f"  Median: {analysis_data[column_name].median():.4f}")
        print(f"  Std Dev: {analysis_data[column_name].std():.4f}")
        print(f"  Min: {analysis_data[column_name].min():.4f}")
        print(f"  Max: {analysis_data[column_name].max():.4f}")
    else:
        mode_val = analysis_data[column_name].mode().iloc[0] if not analysis_data[column_name].mode().empty else "No mode"
        print(f"{column_name} Statistics:")
        print(f"  Mode: {mode_val}")
        print(f"  Unique values: {analysis_data[column_name].nunique()}")
        print(f"  Value counts:")
        for val, count in analysis_data[column_name].value_counts().head().items():
            print(f"    {val}: {count}")
    
    # Death Flag is always treated as categorical
    target_mode = analysis_data[target_col].mode().iloc[0] if not analysis_data[target_col].mode().empty else "No mode"
    print(f"\n{target_col} Statistics:")
    print(f"  Mode: {target_mode}")
    print(f"  Value counts:")
    for val, count in analysis_data[target_col].value_counts().items():
        print(f"    {val}: {count}")
    
    # Create subplots
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=figsize)
    fig.suptitle(f'Analysis: {column_name} vs {target_col}', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
    
    # Since Death Flag is categorical, we only have two cases:
    # Case 1: Column is numeric, Death Flag is categorical
    if col_is_numeric:
        # Box plot
        sns.boxplot(data=analysis_data, x=target_col, y=column_name, ax=axes[0,0])
        axes[0,0].set_title('Box Plot by Death Flag')
        axes[0,0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
        
        # Violin plot
        sns.violinplot(data=analysis_data, x=target_col, y=column_name, ax=axes[0,1])
        axes[0,1].set_title('Violin Plot by Death Flag')
        axes[0,1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
        
        # Bar plot of means
        means = analysis_data.groupby(target_col)[column_name].mean()
        means.plot(kind='bar', ax=axes[1,0])
        axes[1,0].set_title(f'Mean {column_name} by {target_col}')
        axes[1,0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
        
        # Distribution of column by Death Flag category
        for category in analysis_data[target_col].unique():
            subset = analysis_data[analysis_data[target_col] == category][column_name]
            axes[1,1].hist(subset, alpha=0.7, label=f'{target_col}={category}', bins=20)
        axes[1,1].set_title(f'{column_name} Distribution by {target_col}')
        axes[1,1].legend()
        
        # Statistical test
        groups = [group[column_name].values for name, group in analysis_data.groupby(target_col)]
        if len(groups) == 2:
            stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(groups[0], groups[1])
            test_name = 't-test'
        else:
            stat, p_val = stats.f_oneway(*groups)
            test_name = 'ANOVA'
        
        print(f"\nSTATISTICAL ANALYSIS:")
        print("-" * 30)
        print(f"Test: {test_name}")
        print(f"Statistic: {stat:.4f}")
        print(f"P-value: {p_val:.4f}")
        print(f"Significant: {'Yes' if p_val < 0.05 else 'No'}")
        
        # Group statistics
        print(f"\nGROUP STATISTICS:")
        print("-" * 20)
        for group_name, group_data in analysis_data.groupby(target_col):
            group_stats = group_data[column_name]
            print(f"{target_col} = {group_name}:")
            print(f"  Count: {len(group_stats)}")
            print(f"  Mean: {group_stats.mean():.4f}")
            print(f"  Median: {group_stats.median():.4f}")
            print(f"  Std Dev: {group_stats.std():.4f}")
    
    # Case 2: Both categorical
    else:
        # Contingency table heatmap
        contingency_table = pd.crosstab(analysis_data[target_col], analysis_data[column_name])
        sns.heatmap(contingency_table, annot=True, fmt='d', ax=axes[0,0], cmap='Blues')
        axes[0,0].set_title('Contingency Table Heatmap')
        
        # Stacked bar chart
        contingency_table.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, ax=axes[0,1])
        axes[0,1].set_title('Stacked Bar Chart')
        axes[0,1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
        
        # Percentage stacked bar chart
        contingency_pct = contingency_table.div(contingency_table.sum(axis=1), axis=0)
        contingency_pct.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, ax=axes[1,0])
        axes[1,0].set_title('Percentage Stacked Bar Chart')
        axes[1,0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
        
        # Count plot
        sns.countplot(data=analysis_data, x=column_name, hue=target_col, ax=axes[1,1])
        axes[1,1].set_title('Count Plot by Category')
        axes[1,1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
        
        # Chi-square test
        chi2, p_val, dof, expected = stats.chi2_contingency(contingency_table)

analyze_single_column(df, 'Age')

def analyze_single_column(df, column_name, target_col='Death Flag', figsize=(15, 10)):
    """
    Perform detailed bivariate analysis between a single column and Death Flag
    with beautiful visualizations and comprehensive statistics
    """
    
    # Set style for better looking plots
    plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8')
    sns.set_palette("husl")
    
    # Create analysis dataframe
    analysis_data = df[[target_col, column_name]].dropna()
    
    # Force Death Flag to be treated as categorical
    target_is_numeric = False  # Always treat Death Flag as categorical
    col_is_numeric = pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(analysis_data[column_name])
    
    print(f"=== DETAILED ANALYSIS: {column_name} vs {target_col} ===")
    print("=" * 60)
    
    # Basic descriptive statistics
    print(f"\nDESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS:")
    print("-" * 30)
    
    if col_is_numeric:
        print(f"{column_name} Statistics:")
        print(f"  Mean: {analysis_data[column_name].mean():.4f}")
        print(f"  Median: {analysis_data[column_name].median():.4f}")
        print(f"  Std Dev: {analysis_data[column_name].std():.4f}")
        print(f"  Min: {analysis_data[column_name].min():.4f}")
        print(f"  Max: {analysis_data[column_name].max():.4f}")
    else:
        mode_val = analysis_data[column_name].mode().iloc[0] if not analysis_data[column_name].mode().empty else "No mode"
        print(f"{column_name} Statistics:")
        print(f"  Mode: {mode_val}")
        print(f"  Unique values: {analysis_data[column_name].nunique()}")
        print(f"  Value counts:")
        for val, count in analysis_data[column_name].value_counts().head().items():
            print(f"    {val}: {count}")
    
    # Death Flag is always treated as categorical
    target_mode = analysis_data[target_col].mode().iloc[0] if not analysis_data[target_col].mode().empty else "No mode"
    print(f"\n{target_col} Statistics:")
    print(f"  Mode: {target_mode}")
    print(f"  Value counts:")
    for val, count in analysis_data[target_col].value_counts().items():
        print(f"    {val}: {count}")
    
    # Create subplots
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=figsize)
    fig.suptitle(f'Analysis: {column_name} vs {target_col}', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold')
    
    # Since Death Flag is categorical, we only have two cases:
    # Case 1: Column is numeric, Death Flag is categorical
    if col_is_numeric:
        # Box plot
        sns.boxplot(data=analysis_data, x=target_col, y=column_name, ax=axes[0,0])
        axes[0,0].set_title('Box Plot by Death Flag')
        axes[0,0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
        
        # Violin plot
        sns.violinplot(data=analysis_data, x=target_col, y=column_name, ax=axes[0,1])
        axes[0,1].set_title('Violin Plot by Death Flag')
        axes[0,1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
        
        # Bar plot of means
        means = analysis_data.groupby(target_col)[column_name].mean()
        means.plot(kind='bar', ax=axes[1,0])
        axes[1,0].set_title(f'Mean {column_name} by {target_col}')
        axes[1,0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
        
        # Distribution of column by Death Flag category
        for category in analysis_data[target_col].unique():
            subset = analysis_data[analysis_data[target_col] == category][column_name]
            axes[1,1].hist(subset, alpha=0.7, label=f'{target_col}={category}', bins=20)
        axes[1,1].set_title(f'{column_name} Distribution by {target_col}')
        axes[1,1].legend()
        
        # Statistical test
        groups = [group[column_name].values for name, group in analysis_data.groupby(target_col)]
        if len(groups) == 2:
            stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(groups[0], groups[1])
            test_name = 't-test'
        else:
            stat, p_val = stats.f_oneway(*groups)
            test_name = 'ANOVA'
        
        print(f"\nSTATISTICAL ANALYSIS:")
        print("-" * 30)
        print(f"Test: {test_name}")
        print(f"Statistic: {stat:.4f}")
        print(f"P-value: {p_val:.4f}")
        print(f"Significant: {'Yes' if p_val < 0.05 else 'No'}")
        
        # Group statistics
        print(f"\nGROUP STATISTICS:")
        print("-" * 20)
        for group_name, group_data in analysis_data.groupby(target_col):
            group_stats = group_data[column_name]
            print(f"{target_col} = {group_name}:")
            print(f"  Count: {len(group_stats)}")
            print(f"  Mean: {group_stats.mean():.4f}")
            print(f"  Median: {group_stats.median():.4f}")
            print(f"  Std Dev: {group_stats.std():.4f}")
    
    # Case 2: Both categorical
    else:
        # Contingency table heatmap
        contingency_table = pd.crosstab(analysis_data[target_col], analysis_data[column_name])
        sns.heatmap(contingency_table, annot=True, fmt='d', ax=axes[0,0], cmap='Blues')
        axes[0,0].set_title('Contingency Table Heatmap')
        
        # Stacked bar chart
        contingency_table.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, ax=axes[0,1])
        axes[0,1].set_title('Stacked Bar Chart')
        axes[0,1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
        
        # Percentage stacked bar chart
        contingency_pct = contingency_table.div(contingency_table.sum(axis=1), axis=0)
        contingency_pct.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, ax=axes[1,0])
        axes[1,0].set_title('Percentage Stacked Bar Chart')
        axes[1,0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
        
        # Count plot

        axes[1,1].set_title('Count Plot by Category')
        axes[1,1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
        
        # Chi-square test
        chi2, p_val, dof, expected = stats.chi2_contingency(contingency_table)

        axes[1,0].set_title('Percentage Stacked Bar Chart')
        axes[1,0].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
        
        # Count plot
        sns.countplot(data=analysis_data, x=column_name, hue=target_col, ax=axes[1,1])
        axes[1,1].set_title('Count Plot by Category')
        axes[1,1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)
        
        # Chi-square test
        chi2, p_val, dof, expected = stats.chi2_contingency(contingency_table)
        
analyze_single_column(df, 'Face Amount')

# Multivarite Visualization within each type of variable

target = 'Death Flag'  
id_col = df.columns[0]  # First column is ID

# Exclude ID and target from predictor lists
data = df.drop(columns=[id_col]).copy()

numeric_cols = [
    c for c in data.select_dtypes(include=np.number).columns
    if c != target
]

categorical_cols = [
    c for c in data.select_dtypes(
        include=["object", "category", "bool", "string"]
    ).columns
    if c != target
]

# Treat target as categorical for visualization
data[target] = data[target].astype(str)

# 1. Correlation heatmap for numerical predictors only
if len(numeric_cols) >= 2:
    corr = data[numeric_cols].corr(method="spearman")

    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
    sns.heatmap(
        corr, cmap="coolwarm", center=0,
        vmin=-1, vmax=1
    )
    plt.title("Correlation Between Numerical Predictors")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# 2. Pair plot, colored by categorical target
if len(numeric_cols) >= 2:
    selected = numeric_cols
    plot_df = data[selected + [target]].dropna()

    sns.pairplot(
        plot_df,
        vars=selected,
        hue=target,
        corner=True,
        diag_kind="hist"
    )
    plt.show()

# 3. Scatter plot of two numerical predictors by target
if len(numeric_cols) >= 2:
    x_col, y_col = numeric_cols[:2]
    plot_df = data[[x_col, y_col, target]].dropna()

    if len(plot_df) > 5000:
        plot_df = plot_df.sample(5000, random_state=42)

    plt.figure(figsize=(9, 6))
    sns.scatterplot(
        data=plot_df, x=x_col, y=y_col,
        hue=target, alpha=0.6
    )
    plt.title(f"{x_col} vs {y_col}, by {target}")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# 4. Categorical combinations by proportion of class 1

from itertools import combinations

# Analyze every pair of categorical predictors
for cat1, cat2 in combinations(categorical_cols, 2):

    table_df = data[[cat1, cat2, target]].dropna().copy()

    # Keep the 10 most frequent categories per variable
    top1 = table_df[cat1].value_counts().head(10).index
    top2 = table_df[cat2].value_counts().head(10).index

    table_df = table_df[
        table_df[cat1].isin(top1) &
        table_df[cat2].isin(top2)
    ].copy()

    # Proportion of target class 1
    table_df["positive_event"] = (
        table_df[target].astype(str) == "1"
    ).astype(int)

    rates = table_df.pivot_table(
        index=cat1,
        columns=cat2,
        values="positive_event",
        aggfunc="mean"
    )

    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))
    sns.heatmap(
        rates,
        annot=True,
        fmt=".1%",
        cmap="YlOrRd",
        vmin=0,
        vmax=1
    )
    plt.title(f"Proportion of {target}=1: {cat1} vs {cat2}")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
